'''Matchmaking''' ---- '''Matchmaking''' is a system in Tower Defense Simulator that matches up players between servers. Players will be matched up with other players who selected the same mode and squad size. They are also initially matched up based on their [[Level]] and age group, however, the system will not try to find players of similar [[Level]] forever. After a certain point, it will accept players of lower [[Level]] and higher [[Level]], creating large gaps of [[Level]] between players. In [[PVP]] ranked matches, pairing is based on ELO and age group.
==Usage== [[File:PlaySurvival.png|150px|thumb]] '''Matchmaking''' can be activated in two ways. The main method is using the ''Play'' button in the middle of the screen. A secondary method of matchmaking is using statues placed in the lobby, though they are only used for limited-time events. '''Matchmaking''' is available across all game modes. When accessed this way, in most cases a screen with multiple options will appear. There are five sections in the Matchmaking menu. The first is Survival, which consists of all main game modes ([[Easy Mode|Easy]], [[Casual Mode|Casual]], [[Intermediate Mode|Intermediate]], [[Molten Mode|Molten]], [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]], and [[Frost Mode|Frost]]) as well as [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] modes. The second is Story, which includes all of the chapters and missions available in [[Story Mode]]. The third is [[PVP]], which includes Casual and Ranked Player vs. Player matches. The fourth is Arcade, which includes [[Challenge Trials]] and all special modes ([[Polluted Wasteland II]], [[Badlands II]], and [[Pizza Party]]). The fifth and final one is [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]], which contains the experimental Sandbox Mode. There are also a few other screens. For [[Challenge Maps]], there is no option for it in the main '''Matchmaking''' menu. Instead, it can only be accessed through the [[Quests]] menu. For events that occurred up to the [[Ducky Revenge Event]], the old '''Matchmaking''' menu is used instead, where a small pop-up window will appear with multiple difficulty options if they exist before choosing the player count. After getting through the mode selection, you will be asked to select a player count, ranging from solo to squads. Solo creates a singleplayer match, duo creates a two-player match, trio creates a three-player match and quad creates a four-player match. In [[Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore]] modes, you can only play with up to three players (trios) as quads is unavailable for those modes. In [[PVP]] mode, you can only play by yourself (1v1) or with one other player (2v2) against another team. In [[Sandbox Mode]] and during the [[Halloween 2025 Live Events]], two additional options would appear, with those being a squads option for five players and a mega option for six players. In both cases, the same icon for quads is used. However, the options for five and six players in [[Sandbox Mode]] are locked unless you own the [[Gamepasses|Sandbox Plus+ Gamepass]] and are in a party with other players. In [[PVP]] mode, the usual options are replaced with 1v1, which has the players be in teams consisting of one player only (two players total), and 2v2, where players are in two player teams (four players total). Selecting the player count will then start a player search. If playing in solos or if the [[Party]] size is the same as selected player count, a match will be created instantly. Otherwise, '''Matchmaking''' will begin searching for players of a specific similar statistic: *In majority of cases, it will look players of a similar [[Level]]. This applies to majority of the modes, with all exceptions being listed below. If unable to find players of similar [[Level]] quickly, players of significantly higher or lower [[Level]] will be accepted. *Similar age groups are also considered to ensure that all players in the match are able to see each other's messages. *Ranked [[PVP]] looks for players of similar ELO. If unable to find players of similar ELO quickly, players of significantly higher or lower ELO will be accepted. *[[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode will instantly start the match, regardless if the selected player count actually matches the [[Party]] size. However, it will not wait indefinitely until it finds such players, it will instead pick players with lower [[Levels]]/ELO. Once all players are found, every single player's loadout, level, triumph count and loss count will be displayed, alongside their username and avatar. Matchmaking5.png|Match size selection. Matchmaking4.png|Match found. ==Historical Matchmaking== ===Matchmaking Elevator=== '''Matchmaking Elevator''' refers to a '''Matchmaking''' which was never actually used in-game outside of public tests. It would move the player away from the main lobby into an elevator. '''Matchmaking Elevator''' would put the player inside an elevator with three options, survival, [[Hardcore Mode|hardcore]] and event. After either one is chosen a player count would be chosen, which could be one player, two players, three players, four players or a [[MEGA Servers|MEGA Server]]. A search for players would then begin, where player avatars would start appearing inside the elevator. It would be accessible through a "''Play''" button on the screen. MatchmakingElevator1.png|UI. Tower Defense Simulator OST - Unused Matchmaking Elevator Lobby|Unused music. ===Legacy Event Matchmaking=== '''Legacy Event Matchmaking''' refers to an early version of '''Matchmaking''' used by the [[Solar Eclipse Event]] and [[Duck Hunt Event]]. It was a far more primitive version of '''Matchmaking''', as it had no actual options for the player. The match size would always be the highest one available (quads), meaning that if the [[Party]] was not full, the game would fill out the rest of the slots with other players. In [[v1.4.0]], roughly five months after the [[Duck Hunt Event]] had concluded, the game would receive proper '''Matchmaking''' statues in the lobby which would use a slightly different UI and give the player the option to pick the match size. Because of this change, '''Legacy Event Matchmaking''' did not end up being used for the [[Violent Night Event]]. LegacyEventMM4.png|[[Party]] pop up.
